newsitem.title: USA: Armey keeps up his fight against arts body.
newsitem.headline: Armey keeps up his fight against arts body.

text.p: House Majority Leader Dick Armey said Tuesday he will continue to fight for elimination of the National Endowment for the Arts, long a target of conservatives.

In a letter to NEA Chairman Jane Alexander, the Texas Republican said: "It would be fiscally irresponsible to continue this programme, which robs the poor to entertain the rich, when other programmes have a much greater claim to both need and effectiveness."
Foes and allies of the agency are battling over its future as Congress debates a $136 million budget request for the 1998 fiscal year, up from the $99 million appropriated in the current year.
The NEA has been in the centre of controversy in past years over its support for what critics have called pornography.
Armey, who has opposed the NEA since the 1980s, told Alexander that recent media coverage might have led her to believe that funding "is virtually assured."
But he said: "I am writing to advise you of my intent to continue pursuing elimination of the NEA.

"The president has requested a 40 percent increase in funding for the NEA, and less than a 2 percent increase in funding for the National Institutes of Health. This request simply does not reflect the priorities of the American people or of this Congress," Armey said.
He said he was confident that private support could more than replace government funding.
